title: Differentiating `clamp` with respect to a scalar bound of an array raises
description: If the operand `x` of `lax.clamp` is an array and a bound is a scalar,
forward and reverse mode with respect to that bound raise a `TypeError`.
Differentiating with respect to `x` alone works, and so does differentiating `jnp.clip` with respect to a bound.
expected: `lax.clamp` accepts bounds `min` and `max` that are scalars or have the shape of `x`,
and its own batching rule produces scalar bounds.
The derivative with respect to a scalar bound should be what `jnp.clip` computes:
each entry of `x` that the bound clamps contributes 1.
reproducer: # Differentiating with respect to x works.
# Near these bounds the sum is lo + 0.5 + hi, so its gradient in each bound is 1,
# Differentiating lax.clamp with respect to a scalar bound raises.
# actual:  TypeError: select cases must have the same shapes, got [(3,), ()].
# actual:  TypeError: select cases must have the same shapes, got [(3,), ()].
# actual:  TypeError: select cases must have the same shapes, got [(3,), ()].
cause: The JVP rules for `min` and `max` end in `select(pred, g, _zeros(operand))`,
where the tangent `g` has the shape of the bound and `_zeros(operand)` the shape of `x`.
For a scalar bound the shapes differ, and `select_n` raises.
fix: Broadcast `g` to the shape of `x` in the JVP rules, and sum it back in their transposes.
lean: The shape check of `select` is a proof argument of the rules for scalar bounds,
`Jax.Lax.clampJvpScalar_not_defined` shows that it does not follow from the shape checks of `clamp`,
and `Jax.Lax.clampJvpScalar_defined_iff` that it holds exactly when `x` has rank 0.
